recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if FHIR-I reopens the broader pattern[x] behavior on repeating elements; that topic is outside FHIR-33316 and already audited under FHIR-36700.
issue_request: FHIR-33316 was Published/Persuasive for R5 as a non-substantive FHIR-I clarification. It asked to remove the stray word "array" from the ElementDefinition.pattern[x] sentence, changing "each element provided in the pattern[x] array" to "each element provided in the pattern[x]".
initial_application: The exact correction appears in historical commit 08d840fb48809b6e69bfd75e45073818aab41498, "FHIR-33316 Clarify behavior of pattern[x] on arrays", which removed "array" from the build-scoped source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml pattern[x] definition. The broader surrounding wording and examples were introduced by the related FHIR-36700 commit 44ed2366be24968481e1dc367d04cff3be43df0d.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is an active datatype, maps to the ElementDefinition page, and is normative in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-36700 is the same-change-family follow-up for the substantive repeating-element behavior and is already represented on the combined branch by 5be5bbdc1b327e8d006ff1fc0e31473431916e2c. FHIR-28126 later added the optional-element qualifier "if the element has a value", which explains current wording beyond the original FHIR-33316 typo fix.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The latest combined branch source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml already says "each element provided in the pattern[x] must (recursively) match at least one element from the instance array" and no longer contains the targeted "pattern[x] array" wording.

related_jiras.note: Later published clarification spun off from the pattern[x] array confusion; it added each-occurrence wording, all-repetitions behavior, slicing guidance, and examples, and is already audited on the combined branch.
Published clarification that fixed/pattern values on min=0 elements apply only when the element is present, explaining the current "if the element has a value" wording.
